references.text: These verses show the immediate response to the warning in verse 19, where some feared the Lord's word and brought their servants and livestock inside, while others ignored the warning.
The fulfillment of the warning: hail struck down everything in the field, both people and animals, just as the Lord had warned.
A similar warning to gather what belongs to you from the field before destruction comes, in connection with the ark of the covenant.
The locust plague also threatens what remains in the field, continuing the theme of protecting what is out in the open country.
Isaiah refers to God's judgment with hail and urges the people to listen to the Lord's warning.
In Revelation, great hail falls from heaven as God's judgment, an eschatological parallel to the hail plague in Egypt.
Clear narrative parallel: A warning to flee from 'the field/plains' to avoid immediate destruction.
Theological contrast: Letting animals out (life) after the flood versus bringing them in (rescue) before the hail plague.
Theological parallel: Boundaries set by God where crossing them (staying in the field/touching the mountain) leads to death.
